summary:
FOURTEEN assigned items. TWELVE closed by two new refusals in src/fabric/api.py::build plus one in src/spine/derive.py::operating_population; ONE (FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=0) is a GENUINE CONFLICT and is deferred with the exact edits; ONE (the 26 int levers at +/-inf) was already fixed in src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce before this round and is re-verified here.

WHAT LANDED.
(1) THE NON-FINITE REFUSAL, WIDENED FROM ELEVEN NAMED LEVERS TO EVERY FLOAT LEVER THE PACKAGE DECLARES. The old block was `v != v or v == float('inf')` over eleven hand-typed names, and the comment beside it LISTED the six it declined to check -- FAB_ALPHA, FAB_ROUTE_T, FAB_HALT_MAX, FAB_BAL_FLOOR, FAB_SPAWN_FLOOR, FAB_ROUTE_REGION_W. Five of those six carried the identical defect. build() now enumerates FAB's own float levers through spine/lever.py::Config.keys and ::Config.lever -- the spine's own introspection, so the OWNED env name in the message is GENERATED and not typed, and a float lever added tomorrow is covered with no second list to go stale -- and refuses any that is not math.isfinite. NO DECLINED LIST REMAINS: the 26 int levers are refused at nan (ValueError) and at +/-inf (OverflowError) by spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce under their own owned names, the 12 bools coerce every spelling, and the one str lever carries choices= plus the NotBuilt refusal. 43 + 26 + 12 + 1 = 82, the whole declaration set.
(2) A FLOOR OF ONE ON SIX COUNTS -- FAB_N0, FAB_SLOTS, FAB_RANK, FAB_DK, FAB_EMB_HID, FAB_HOPS -- refused together, before anything is derived from them, each quoting its own measurement. No finiteness rule could ever have reached these: all six are finite ints that pass every type check. FAB_DEPTH0 is deliberately NOT among them because 0 is its DECLARED sentinel.
(3) src/spine/derive.py::operating_population now refuses a non-finite pressure by name of the QUANTITY. That placement is forced: FAB_PRESSURE is consumed by the FAB.d_operating_population coupling DURING spine/assemble.py::build, before any Config is frozen, so FAB.build's own finiteness refusal cannot see it. The refusal states that it cannot name the lever and why (two packages' couplings reach that function) -- the same gap tests/test_fabric.py::check_f8_manage_period_kind_and_refusal reports per layer for flush_period_windows.

COMPLETE CENSUS, MEASURED TWICE AND AGREEING, ZERO MISSES. Once in-process with _reopen_assembly()+reset_issued() before every assemble.build (the sanctioned alternative), and once with a FRESH SUBPROCESS PER CELL -- 250 processes. Both runs:
  FLOAT levers 43: refused BY NAME at nan/inf/-inf 129/129; rebuilt at own default 43/43
  INT levers 26: refused BY OWNED NAME at spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce 78/78
  SIX COUNTS: each refused at 0 and each building at 1

WHAT THESE REFUSALS DO NOT CLAIM, AND NO DOCSTRING IN THE DIFF SAYS OTHERWISE. They close four values per float lever and one arm of six counts. They BOUND NOTHING. FAB_ALPHA=1e26 is finite, returns aux 0.5150710 and composed 2.943258 -- a pair no report would flag -- over a population whose gradient tensors are already 15/23 poisoned, which is WORSE than +inf because +inf at least comes back nan. Every one of the three files says this in as many words. A declared per-lever domain is the general answer and is recorded as the owner's open question.

THE max/min RE-GREP ASKED FOR. Every max( and min( in src/fabric/api.py was re-read against the declared lever types. Exactly FOUR sites take a FLOAT LEVER as an argument, and the three the sweep named are three of them: `max(1e-3, route_t)` in _entry_logits AND in _halt_logit (two sites, one lever), `max(floor, ...)` in _decay_to_floor (FAB_BAL_FLOOR), and `max(spawn_mult*typ, spawn_floor)` in _spawn_check (two levers). There is NO fifth: every other max/min in the file takes ints or counts, and an int lever cannot hold a nan. All four are now closed at build, and each site's docstring carries the mechanism (Python's max keeps its FIRST argument when the comparison is False; every comparison with NaN is False) plus what is STILL open at a finite value.

ONE THING I WAS ASKED TO DO AND DID NOT, WHICH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE HERE. derive.flush_period_windows was NOT changed to refuse `< 1`. tests/test_fabric.py::check_f8_manage_period_kind_and_refusal pins FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=0 as legal IN WORDS -- 'ZERO IS DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED by either refusal, and this check holds them to that: 0 must assemble and return Windows(0)' -- and asserts it in code. The 575-case oracle in tests/test_derive.py does NOT pin it (there is no flush_period_windows table in .rework/oracle/ and the only 0-related case is `flush_period_windows(Windows(8), 16) == Flushes(1)`, which is the OUTPUT floor and survives the change untouched). So the conflict is with test_fabric, not the oracle. PROVEN on a patched COPY of the tree at /tmp: with `< 1` in place, test_fabric does not merely fail, it dies with an uncaught UnitError at its line 1360 inside `cfg(FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=0)`. tests/ is not mine to edit, so the exact find/replace for BOTH files is in `unfinished`; they must land together.

SUITE AFTER: identical to the stated baseline, 0 failing everywhere. Three files changed, all three mine; nothing under tests/, runs/ or docs/ touched.

findings.detail: `cap = max(n0, slots)` is the declared arithmetic and a cap of n0 is a fine answer, so this is refused for the SETPOINT it derives and not for the pool. spine/derive.py::operating_population carries `n = max(3, n)` -- its own docstring calls it the same floor as the gate's n_live <= 2 -- and then returns `min(n_slots, n) if n_slots >= 3 else n_slots`, so below three slots the floor is bypassed and at 0 the answer is 0. THE REFUSAL IS FAB'S AND NOT THE CONVERSION'S, deliberately: derive is RIGHT at slots=2 and is pinned there by the oracle (`operating_population(0.45, 2) == 2`, 'two slots is all there is'), so a guard in derive would either break that pin or be a second, differently-worded rule. FAB.build can name the lever, and does.

findings.detail: Was REFUSED_BADLY: the only float lever in this package whose bad value was caught at all, and caught BY ACCIDENT -- `n = int(exact)` inside spine/derive.py::operating_population. FAB.build's new finiteness rule cannot reach it: the FAB.d_operating_population coupling runs during spine/assemble.py::build, before any Config is frozen. So the refusal is derive's, added in front of `int(exact)`, naming the SETPOINT it was computing. It states plainly that it cannot name the lever and why -- two packages' couplings (FAB.d_operating_population and CAP.d_operating_population) reach that one function, so a lever name written in there would be wrong for one of them. That naming gap is reported, not claimed away.

unfinished.title: FOUR FINITE NEGATIVES ARE THE SAME REVERSED-TERM CLASS THE ELEVEN ARE REFUSED FOR, AND ARE NOW MEASURED BUT NOT REFUSED
unfinished.reason: A refusal is a RULING and this round's was the finiteness one. What I would not leave standing is the sentence that used to sit in build() claiming these were unmeasured -- I measured them and the numbers are now in the file beside the decision not to act on them. The next ruling has the data it needs.
unfinished.detail:
Driven one at a time at the harness base over two forward passes, against aux 0.5134152173995972 and sum|g|max 1.3968892609970744:
  FAB_HALT_MAX=-0.9       sum|g|max 2.5214699913394156, aux 0.5134174823760986. `raw.clamp(max=-0.9)` makes the halted mass NEGATIVE, so `alive = alive * (1 - ph)` AMPLIFIES the residual instead of damping it. A ceiling that becomes a negative mass -- the worst of the eight and, on the gradient reading, worse than FAB_HALT_MAX=+inf.
  FAB_ROUTE_REGION_W=-1.0 aux 0.5095041990280151, sum|g|max 1.202592107085124. The region term with its sign REVERSED: routing scored toward the experts whose region is LEAST like the material.
  FAB_BAL_FLOOR=-0.15     bit-identical to the baseline at step_windows=1; at step_windows=100000 aux 0.48843273520469666 against 0.4970445930957794. The bounded form of the -inf sign inversion, and equally late-arriving.
  FAB_ALPHA=-0.5          sum|g|max 1.3063406257114876, aux unchanged (alpha is not an aux term). The residual step runs BACKWARD, h moving away from the mixture.
  FAB_PRESSURE=-0.45      operating_population answers 3 -- its own floor -- for a setpoint with no reading, and cull_gate_open is then true at every occupancy.
  FAB_ROUTE_T=-0.1, FAB_SPAWN_FLOOR=-0.02, FAB_MUT=-0.25: INERT, bit-identical to the baseline in aux, in sum|g|max and in every counter (the first two floored by a `max` at their point of use, the third with no live reader).
That is the SAME split the eleven already-refused magnitude levers have -- some reverse, some are exactly 'off' and only misreport -- which is the argument for extending the negative refusal to FAB_HALT_MAX, FAB_ROUTE_REGION_W, FAB_BAL_FLOOR and FAB_ALPHA. Refusing the three inert ones would remove no configuration either, on the same ground capacity gives for CAP_LIFT. Not taken here; the measurements are in src/fabric/api.py::build beside the existing negative refusal.

unfinished.detail: `limit = max(int(dom_min), int(dom_frac * max(1, int(live_domains))))` in src/fabric/api.py::_breadth_ban. dom_min's declared purpose is 'the floor that stops int(0.10 * small_n) collapsing to zero and banning every expert from every domain it does not already hold'; at 0 the floor is gone, limit is 0, and `len(pop.dom_of[e]) >= 0` is true for EVERY expert, so the cap would mask the entire population out of routing -- caught only incidentally by the `if int(ban.sum()) < n` guard, which then switches the cap off completely rather than reporting it. Measured today: Gate fab.breadth_cap: UNREACHABLE (limit=0 of live_domains=3 vs dom_frac=0.1, dom_min=0), against limit=4 at the default. FAB_DOM_FRAC=0 is the DECLARED way to switch the cap off, so dom_min=0 has no reading of its own. It is a seventh candidate for the floor-of-one refusal I added, and I did not add it because it is a mechanism with no live reader and the floor-of-one message quotes a measurement for each of its six.

The general answer to all of it is a declared per-lever domain (lo/hi in the shape `choices=` already has), which is the owner's open question and which I have recorded as open in all three files rather than pre-empted.
